source: BLM Mineral & Land Records System (MLRS), Land Tenure Case layer, product SMALL TRACT

places.name: Wonder Valley
places.blurb: The long, open basin east of Twentynine Palms along Amboy Road, where the five-acre grid runs nearly unbroken to the Sheep Hole Mountains.

places.name: Twentynine Palms
places.blurb: The oasis town where desert homesteading for health began after the First World War, and the reason the Small Tract Act was written.

places.name: Desert Heights
places.blurb: The mesa north-west of Twentynine Palms, one of the densest blocks of small tracts anywhere in the desert.

places.name: Sunfair & Copper Mountain Mesa
places.blurb: The open flats and mesa between Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms, north of the highway and the dry lake.

places.name: Indian Cove & Panorama Heights
places.blurb: South of the highway between Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms, under the Wonderland of Rocks.

places.name: Joshua Tree
places.blurb: Tracts climb north from the village toward the mesa, a few miles from the national park boundary.

places.name: Yucca Valley & Yucca Mesa
places.blurb: The largest town in the basin, with small tracts spread across the mesa to its north.

places.name: Landers
places.blurb: Homestead Valley: a broad, quiet spread of cabins north of Yucca Valley.

places.name: Flamingo Heights
places.blurb: A shelf of high desert along Old Woman Springs Road between Yucca Valley and Landers.

places.name: Johnson Valley
places.blurb: The far north-west edge of the basin, where the tracts thin out toward the dry lakes.

places.name: Pioneertown & Rimrock
places.blurb: Boulder country above Yucca Valley, on the road to the old movie-set town.

places.name: Morongo Valley
places.blurb: The first valley up the grade from the low desert, at the western door of the basin.

places.name: Lucerne Valley
places.blurb: A wide dry-lake valley on the north slope of the San Bernardino Mountains.

places.name: Old Woman Springs
places.blurb: East of Lucerne Valley, near the spring that gave the highway its name.

places.name: Apple Valley
places.blurb: East of the Mojave River, where five-acre tracts were patented alongside a booming postwar resort town.

places.name: Hesperia & Baldy Mesa
places.blurb: The mesa at the top of the Cajon Pass, the closest small tracts to Los Angeles.

places.name: Phelan & Piñon Hills
places.blurb: Joshua tree and juniper country along the north foot of the San Gabriel Mountains.

places.name: El Mirage
places.blurb: Scattered tracts around the dry lake at the county's western edge.

places.name: Victorville & Adelanto
places.blurb: The Mojave River towns at the center of the Victor Valley.

places.name: Helendale
places.blurb: Along the Mojave River and old Route 66 between Victorville and Barstow.

places.name: Shadow Mountains
places.blurb: Creosote flats along Highway 395 north of Adelanto.

places.name: Barstow & Lenwood
places.blurb: A dense block of tracts on the slope south of the railroad town.

places.name: Daggett & Yermo
places.blurb: Old mining and railroad stops along the river east of Barstow.

places.name: Stoddard Valley
places.blurb: Along Barstow Road, in the empty country between Lucerne Valley and Barstow.

places.name: Trona & Searles Valley
places.blurb: A company town on the edge of Searles Lake, surveyed from the Mount Diablo Meridian.

places.name: Baker
places.blurb: A highway stop on the road to Las Vegas at the foot of the Baker Grade.

places.name: Needles & the Colorado River
places.blurb: The river towns on the Arizona line.
